verdict: Leads are flowing at low cost; pipeline intake and profile visibility need attention.
narrative: Over the last 28 days, you received 153 leads from paid social at a cost of $12.69 per lead — well below the historical range of $19–45 — so the campaign itself is performing. Week-over-week, spend rose 12% while leads grew only 5%, which nudged cost per lead slightly higher; that softening is being watched but is not a concern at current levels. More immediately, your Google Business Profile went dark over the last four days, cutting off organic calls and direction requests that would normally warm up inbound prospects; restoring that profile cadence is the priority this week. Separately, 24 leads that arrived through ads are not yet showing up in the pipeline, meaning they have not been followed up as tracked opportunities — that gap is an intake issue, not an ads issue, and it is being addressed now. Next period you should see the profile active again and lead-to-pipeline tracking tightened.

highlights.phrase: leads received in the last 28 days from paid social
cost per lead this period, well below your historical baseline
Google Business Profile actions this period, though zero in the last 4 days

watch_item.issue: 24 leads from this period are unaccounted for in your pipeline, and none have converted to a tracked opportunity — a sign that intake handoff is breaking down.
watch_item.fix: We are closing the gap between ad leads and pipeline contacts this week and ensuring every incoming lead is logged and followed up.
